question: A 28-year-old primigravida presents to the office with complaints of heartburn while lying flat on the bed at night and mild constipation that started a couple of weeks ago. She is 10 weeks pregnant, as determined by her last menstrual period. Her first menstruation was at 13 years of age and she has always had regular 28-day cycles. Her past medical history is insignificant. She does not smoke cigarettes or drink alcohol and does not take any medications. Her father died of colon cancer at 70 years of age, while her mother has diabetes and hypertension. Her vital signs include: temperature 36.9℃ (98.4℉), blood pressure 98/52 mm Hg, pulse 113/minute, oxygen saturation 99%, and respiratory rate 12 /minute. The physical examination was unremarkable, except for a diastolic murmur heard over the apex. Which of the following is considered abnormal in this woman?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pregnancy" -> "increased blood volume" -> "increased cardiac output" -> "possible diastolic murmur" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Pregnancy" -> "decreased vascular resistance" -> "compensatory mechanisms" -> "normal physiological changes" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Pregnancy" -> "low blood pressure" -> "possible concern" -> "could indicate hypovolemia" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Diastolic murmur" -> "common in pregnancy" -> "not necessarily abnormal" -> "requires further evaluation" -> 70%
analysis: In a pregnant woman, physiological changes include decreased vascular resistance and increased cardiac output, which are normal adaptations to support the growing fetus. A diastolic murmur can be common in pregnancy due to increased blood volume and flow. However, low blood pressure (98/52 mm Hg) and tachycardia (pulse of 113/min) can be concerning, especially if they are symptomatic. In this case, the low blood pressure is particularly notable as it may indicate inadequate perfusion, especially in the context of her symptoms. Therefore, low blood pressure is considered abnormal in this woman.
